channel.title: Tectonic Watchers
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Tectonic Watchers" - The unexplained "Earthquake Lights" are actually entities watching these earthquakes.

item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
Hello! Thank you for responding so quickly!

1) I worded it poorly. I edited the document and made it so that it specifies that it's a regular SCP, however with more of a narrative structure (think SCP-5000).

2) That makes sense to me. I'll make them non-humanoid, I'd just need to think of a shape. Perhaps some form of indescribable or incomprehensible shape, similar to a Lovecraftian monster? This'd make sense, due to the update I created.

3) The agent will probably be gone for around 7~ months, to gain a full understanding of the society of the place. However, as I stated in my revised version, they cause another large earthquake which is when he is returned to make a peace treaty.

4) Yeah, that made no sense. I ended up completely removing that.

5) I added this in the revised version of my idea, which is:

These entities don't wish to create and spectate the chaos which happens, however as if an addiction they depend on it. It is unknown whether they die if there is no chaos spectated. These light creatures are entities born from dying stars, and as such are naturally attracted towards extremely chaotic events, living off of the chaos. Due to the fact that it's one of the few places which are inhabited, these entities seem to enjoy the chaos which comes with this. When times are extremely boring, they seem to create their own manual disasters, usually by moving tectonic plates and creating earthquakes. as they're the easiest to create.

6) I also gave reasoning for this, which is stated above.

There are also many other things which I changed about it. Thank you very much, once again!

item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
Hello! Thank you for answering!

+ show block
– hide block

I worded it poorly. I edited the document and made it so that it specifies that it's a regular SCP, however with more of a narrative structure (think SCP-5000).
I changed it so that the MTF Unit shows development by originally only interacting with the entities for research purposes, however slowly grows to empathize with the fact that they regret their nature. They seem to take a strong interest in the mental functions of these SCPs, leading to an SCP Article with purposefully too much detail - the final draft edited by scientists cuts out much more detail than what is present during it.
I've added a new paragraph detailing the reasoning and secrets behind the entities, which are as follows.

These entities don't wish to create and spectate the chaos which happens, however as if an addiction they depend on it. It is unknown whether they die if there is no chaos spectated. These light creatures are entities born from dying stars, and as such are naturally attracted towards extremely chaotic events, living off of the chaos. Due to the fact that it's one of the few places which are inhabited, these entities seem to enjoy the chaos which comes with this. When times are extremely boring, they seem to create their own manual disasters, usually by moving tectonic plates and creating earthquakes. as they're the easiest to create.

To make the MTF Unit have more development & reasons to care, I gave them a slight amount of backstory explained in this quote.

He empathizes, as he was originally a drug addict who severely struggled to break his addiction. He gains motivation to learn more about them to try and find a way to have the foundation assist in this 'chaos'-addiction, as that's what he always wished he had. This also motivates him to write more so the foundation can understand as much as they can.

It took me a moment to think of a good hook, however I decided on one. It'd be the fact that these creatures seem to have a society, and people they care about, along with emotions and feeling. It gives a side to them other than just 'chaos-lovers'. Diving deeper into the sociability & lives of these creatures which have been created on a foundation of misery & chaos could prove extremely interesting.

item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
1) Is this one article or two? Like when you say it goes from tale to SCP… do you mean it starts in this document and then connects to another, OR are you saying it will start as prose and then you'll take the SCP formatting in the middle of the tale, and then switch back to tale prose?

2) I find the fact that these light entities are humanoid to be a bit boring, these seem remarkably alien in every other respect… so why make them humanoid?

3) I'm not sure if you're aware but earthquakes bad enough to wreck cities aren't common occurrence, is this agent going to be taken away for an extremely long time?

4) "Finally, when he's freed, he decides to watch one final earthquake with them. That's how it'd end, with a full log & a destroyed city." -> I don't really understand why he would want to do this? What does he get out of it? Also, its fairly coldblooded when he could warn people of an impending earthquake bad enough to destroy a city

5) "The man would slowly begin to communicate with these entities, finding out more and more about them - as the secrets reveal he continually updates the logs manually." Seems to be that the entire article will revolve around this… and you've left it out of your proposal. What is the secret? What are these things? Why do they want to "watch" earthquakes?

6) Finally, I don't really understand why they are made of light? Doesn't seem thematically connected to the concepts of earthquakes at all

item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
[PM request acknowledged, consider this a placeholder]- will critique shortly :)

Hello Identity8866! let's take a look :)

+ show block
– hide block

Page Layout (Optional): It'd begin as a tale. After a medium amount of writing in the tale, it'd then show an entry of the SCP - at least, what is understood about them at that point. Then switching back to tale, then after more is learnt, the document is updated again. Repeat this until the document is fully written, ending with a short note.

While I'm not the best person to ask (or use as reference) by any means on formats. I don't really see the reason this needs to cater to a tale and an SCP article? -While the narrative does show a character writing/updating the article in the field, they don't seem to have clear motivation to do so? I feel for this to work better they need more than just "its their job", as motivation.

Elevator Pitch: An unexplained (yet theorized) scientific phenomena referred to as "Earthquake lights". Strange lights that seem to appear in the skies whilst (usually high-magnitude) earthquakes form. However, what isn't expected is that these are entities made of light, appearing to simply spectate the earthquakes. Why they do this is found out in the tale.

Central Narrative: During a high-magnitude earthquake near Site [REDACTED], there were "Earthquake Lights" spotted by many people. As this is a scientifically unexplained phenomena, MTF Unit Rho-10 "Shaken, Not Stirred" (an MTF unit created to withstand seismic activity, or unnatural geological movement) enters the scene to investigate. After recordings are taken, and the film is placed through numerous filters & analysations, it's found that each of these 'strobes' of light contain a nearly humanoid entity which seems to be watching the earthquakes. When another high-magnitude earthquake occurs near the same area within the next month, the same dispatch is sent to investigate these flashes of light closer. As the protagonist, codename "Charlie-0" (or C-0 by military alphabets) approaches towards the light, it seems to remain still for much longer than previous. They go to the top of the nearest destroyed building via an extremely long grappling hook and a lot of climbing. 23 minutes later, they arrive at the top, before the entity slowly floats down towards him. They take him somewhere - yet to be discovered. The man would slowly begin to communicate with these entities, finding out more and more about them - as the secrets reveal he continually updates the logs manually. Finally, when he's freed, he decides to watch one final earthquake with them. That's how it'd end, with a full log & a destroyed city.

So overall, theres a bit of missing clarification here. The entities 'secrets' and motives don't really get revealed or mentioned much, which makes it hard for me to gauge wether or not the payoff works with the rest of the narrative and concept. As it stands, the narrative feels a bit anticlimactic as there isn't any closure to what the skips are doing or why.

Along with this, the character himself isn't really developed (at least not from what I can see), which makes it hard to get invested emotionally in the narrative as whole, as he is more or less a random MTF to the audience.- what are his motives? why does he want to update the logs? does he go through any major conflicts? what will make me as the reader care about this character?

Its also oddly convenient to me that this activity happened in the same place, in a very short time frame, and the Foundation just happened to notice there was anomaly.- Generally speaking, the earthquakes don't seem to bare much of an impact on much? they just sort happen, and theres not real consequences.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact that this could, hypothetically, be real is a big thing. Playing off of real world unexplained phenomena. Not to mention the fact it opens up as a tale-SCP has always caught my interest. A dangerous scenario (that being an earthquake) being traversed whilst also trying to gain intel on things which you can barely even see for more then a flash of a second is extremely difficult, and thrilling to read about.

Dangerous scenarios won't really keep audience attention, if theres nothing to back it conceptually (or narratively for that matter). While I think this premise could defiantly work, there doesn't seem to be enough focus on the actual anomaly and their overall motives here.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques/perspectives in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

RED

item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded: That sounds really interesting and dynamic. So maybe you'll want to expand on why they cause these earthquakes in some way whether that be a flat out answer, a mostly mysterious hint, or what have you. Given that the foundation commonly works to avoid disasters, they likely wouldn't attempt an all-out war without the certain leverage or answers of some other SCPs at the foundation's disposal. I could absolutely see them preparing repair/response teams to either stop/lessen the quakes and/or repair the damages & people and predictions could actually fit really well with that. The most interesting and probably difficult way would be for the Foundation to establish some form of agreement of peace. Remember: Secure, Contain, Protect. Think about what's going into the procedures portion.

item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for responding!

I intend for the MTF unit to originally only stay there to gain more Intel, however slowly come to learn that it's actually an entire race of people which are seemingly god-like. The reason they took him is because he's the first non-light entity to attempt to interact with them in all of history. Of course they know about humans, but not much as they only seem to watch earthquakes or other catastrophic events such as Volcanoes and the like.
He'd slowly figure out most of the information due to inference and suggestion from the entities.
While I haven't directly decided on this 100%, I've been considering the fact that these SCPs are actually revealed to manually move tectonic plates to cause earthquakes, which would be extremely dangerous if they're capable of doing that.
I was considering that due to the nature of the SCPs extreme difficulty to contain and high danger, the SCP Foundation could possibly attempt to even attack the entities whilst they're appearing during an earthquake to neutralize the threat of extreme magnitude seismic activity - (due to specific patterns of locations in which they appear they could possibly predict the location of the next light). That may give the MTF a choice between choosing The Foundation or SCPs. I'd have to decide which they choose from there.
This war could then tie in with the MTF which you mentioned attempting to neutralize the entities seemingly inside of an entire war between these light beings & The Foundation. I'd have to choose how that ends, however. If they're capable of just shifting tectonic plates it could end in a possible XK-Class Scenario, ending the entire world, however I don't know if my first SCP would be allowed to go that far. I'll have to think about the escalation of it a bit more.

Reply to below, as I don't want to further the thread:

You saying that gave me another possible idea that the MTF is actually a "spokesperson" for the light people, and he advocates for the peace between them and delivers messages. I'll continue to think about it as much as I can, as it'd make sense the SCP Foundation wouldn't want to engage war.

item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
In the tale itself, you should probably develop in the writing who the protagonist holds allegiance to as the events unfold. Does he hold sympathy towards them, is he still set on getting them into containment, or is he just waiting it out to get away? Why are the lights telling him all this information?
When it comes to the SCP: What is the danger or interesting aspects of these lights themselves? Is this location the lights take him to also a factor in the SCP? The SCP log would benefit if it contains the Foundation's management of the damages if at all. If the foundation is entirely unable to contain, influence, or mitigate the SCP's exposure to the outside world, it just feels sort of useless to read as part of the SCP foundation unless it's tied into other portions of the foundation. I could see potential tie-ins with SCP-1000, MTF Ghost busters, MTF Mole Rats, MTF City Slickers, and MTF White Rabbits if you're comfortable with them. Make sure to include how they are managed by the foundation to the best or their ability.

After they allow him to leave, he goes to the SCP Foundation with all the logged knowledge, discussion, and updates to the file, explaining everything he's learnt (almost everything there is to know). By the end, the SCP Foundation sends him back as a sort of 'messenger' to attempt to create a peace treaty. After this offering for peace, the SCPs seem to at first oblige. For the next year there are no earthquake lights spectated. However, they seem to continue after this time - seemingly more severe then previously, as if something of a relapse. This'd be a whole 'nother stress for the foundation, and I'd need to choose what they'd do after this. As they're aware they would be unable to defeat these entities, the most they can do is attempt to lower the amount of damage caused by SCP-XXXX-1 related earthquakes, and cover up the phenomena as something which it is not.
